title: Bob Greenblatt Explains Why Viewers Are Returning to Familiar TV Shows
body_md:
Streaming platforms offer an enormous selection of television, yet familiar favorites can be more attractive than the latest premieres. Veteran television producer Bob Greenblatt, currently an executive producer on The Gilded Age, discussed this challenge in an interview with The New York Times. His remarks were reported on November 28, 2026, and offer a useful perspective on the competition between new programming and established television libraries.

## Familiar stories have an advantage

Greenblatt suggested that producing an established hit enjoying renewed popularity through streaming is easier than introducing an entirely new series to the market. With numerous services constantly offering fresh programs, viewers face the difficult task of deciding which stories deserve their time. Returning to a familiar favorite such as Seinfeld or Downton Abbey offers a more predictable experience.

The observation points to a broader challenge beyond nostalgia. From an audience perspective, starting an unfamiliar series involves uncertainty. A viewer may not connect with the characters, enjoy the storytelling, or feel confident that the series will ultimately deliver a satisfying conclusion. Revisiting an established favorite removes much of that uncertainty.

That does not necessarily mean audiences have lost interest in original storytelling. Rather, a new series must provide a compelling reason to choose it over a familiar alternative that has already earned the viewer's trust.

## Viewing figures reflect the trend

According to Luminate figures cited in the report, viewing of older titles across major streaming services increased by more than 40 percent in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the corresponding period a year earlier. Viewing of new television series and movies declined over the same period.

The figure describes a change in viewing, not a 40 percent increase in subscriptions or the market share of older programs. It also does not establish that every platform experienced the same pattern.

Netflix provides a notable example. The first season of Power, the Omari Hardwick drama that originally premiered on Starz in 2014, ranked eighth among the service's most-watched programs for November 16–22. The second and first seasons of Black Doves, the British spy series starring Keira Knightley that debuted in 2024, ranked second and sixth respectively.

## What this means for new television

One possible implication is that streaming libraries have become competitors to new releases rather than merely supplementary programming. A premiere must compete not only with other current productions but also with years of established favorites available on demand.

These figures alone cannot demonstrate that contemporary television has declined in quality. They do, however, illustrate why discovery and audience confidence matter when introducing unfamiliar stories.

Would you rather revisit a beloved television series or take a chance on something entirely new?
